beats.narration: [excited] Drill through a marble, and through the Earth. [curious] Trim both leftover rings to the same height. They hold the same volume.
[thoughtful] It's called the napkin-ring theorem. [confident] Punch a cylinder through any sphere, and the leftover band's volume depends only on its height.

[curious] Slice the ring flat. Each slice is an annulus, sphere outer edge minus cylinder inner edge, and the R-squared cancels. [confident] What's left is pi times h-squared-over-four, minus z-squared. Add the slices, and the ring integrates to pi h cubed over six.
[warm] So a jeweller with a marble, and a giant with a moon. [excited] Same-height rings, same amount of stuff.
